title: Automated MZI Control
description: High-precision arbitrary magnitude/phase setting (7-8 bit resolution) for scalable photonic computing.

title: Consistent Histories Analysis
description: Robert Griffiths applies the consistent histories formalism to the nested MZI, disagreeing with Vaidman's analysis and agreeing with Li et al.

title: Disconnected Trajectories Paradox
description: Nikolaev argues that the weak-measurement results are explained by classical electrodynamics or standard quantum mechanics with continuous paths, challenging Vaidman's 'discontinuous trajectories' reading.

title: Electronic MZI
description: First electronic MZI using edge states in 2D electron gas (QHE regime)—62% visibility, opens path to fractional charge measurement.

title: Elitzur–Vaidman Bomb Tester
description: Introduces interaction-free measurement—detecting object presence without physically interacting, using quantum superposition in MZI.

title: Experimental IFM Realized
description: Kwiat, Weinfurter, Herzog, Zeilinger and Kasevich give a first experimental demonstration of interaction-free measurement with single photons, in a Michelson-type interferometer.

title: Experimental Past Detection
description: Danan, Farfurnik, Bar-Ad and Vaidman experimentally probe the 'past of a photon' in a nested MZI—weak traces appear in paths the photons seemingly did not traverse.

title: Fiber Phase Locking
description: New method for arbitrary-phase locking in fiber MZIs—demonstrated with 99.3% (background-subtracted) two-photon interference visibility for quantum networks.

title: Graphene Electronic MZI
description: First high-visibility (98%) electronic MZI in graphene using spin/valley-polarized edge channels—robust to dephasing.

title: Heisenberg-Scale Estimation
description: Achieves Heisenberg-limited precision for simultaneous two-phase estimation using squeezed + coherent states.

title: Higher Order Weak Values
description: Higher-order weak values for paths in nested MZIs—extends the path-integral approach to weak values to sequences of weak measurements.

title: Mach's Refinement
description: Ludwig Mach refines Zehnder's design, creating stable interference fringes. The apparatus bears both inventors' names.

title: Nanoparticle Matter-Wave Interferometry
description: Matter-wave interference of sodium nanoparticles with over 7,000 atoms in a three-grating interferometer—macroscopicity μ = 15.5, an order of magnitude above previous experiments.

title: Past of a Quantum Particle
description: Vaidman's weak measurement analysis of nested MZI claims 'discontinuous trajectories'—sparking major foundations debate.

title: Quantum Parameter Estimation Limits
description: Critical analysis exposing QFI overoptimism in MZI models—proper constraints needed for realistic experiments.

title: Quantum Trajectories Debate
description: Li, Al-Amri and Zubairy comment on Vaidman's analysis—argue the results align with standard quantum mechanics. Exchange in Phys. Rev. A.

title: Quantum Wavemetry
description: Byoung S. Ham proposes coherence de Broglie wavelength superresolution from the Mth-power unitary of an MZI—loss tolerant without N00N states.

title: Two-Photon Interference
description: Rarity, Tapster et al. demonstrate two-photon interference of entangled photon pairs in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer, showing non-classical correlations.

title: Wave-Particle Duality Test
description: Breaks traditional V² + D² ≤ 1 limit using weak-measurement MZI—achieving V² + D² ≈ 1.63.

title: Zehnder's Original Interferometer
description: Ludwig Zehnder invents the interferometer (Ein neuer Interferenzrefraktor), pioneering beam-splitter design for measuring refractive index variations.

title: Wheeler's Delayed-Choice Experiment
description: Jacques et al. realise Wheeler's delayed-choice gedanken experiment with a single-photon MZI whose second beam splitter is inserted or removed after the photon has entered.

title: Direct Counterfactual Communication Protocol
description: Salih, Li, Al-Amri and Zubairy propose direct counterfactual quantum communication using nested MZIs and the quantum Zeno effect.
